admission.justification: Durable product holding preserves the permission guard and avoids asking a parent or developer to repeat work whose acceptance can be uncertain.

alternatives.option: Take unavailable-recipient work into a bounded recipient-workspace store and deliver it later.

alternatives.option: Refuse unavailable recipients and require parents to resend on later turns.
alternatives.reason: Manual retries have no reliable prompt/turn-ready signal and can duplicate already taken work.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The native host supplies a durable ordered queue with equivalent permission protection and workspace reclamation.

consequences: Waiting text is limited to twenty messages, has no time expiry, and ends with compact receipt custody rather than permanent text retention.
context: A host message at a permission prompt would deny it; between-turn-only recipients also cannot take peers while working.
